bull_thesis: Sylvamo at $37.22 (verified live on the New York listing, 2026-07-21) is priced as if the deliberately awful 2026 transition year is the new normal. The bull case is that 2026 is a manufactured trough, not a run-rate: management guided roughly $65 million of one-time footprint-transition costs (the end of International Paper's Riverdale supply agreement in April 2026 plus an inventory-build bridge), concentrated more than half the year's maintenance-outage cost into the fourth quarter around the $145 million Eastover investments, and still reaffirmed on the May 2026 call that Eastover is on schedule and on budget with the full $50 million annual benefit intact from 2027. As the one-times roll off and Eastover ramps, adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) can recover from a ~$330 million 2026 toward $460-500 million in 2027 — versus $448 million in 2025 and $632 million in 2024. Meanwhile the industry is rationalizing supply faster than demand declines: Georgetown, Chillicothe (-6%) and the Riverdale conversion (-7% of North American capacity) have pushed operating rates toward the mid-90s, imports have fallen back to ~10% of demand, and price increases are being realized across all three regions. The balance sheet supports patience: about 1.6 times levered, the 2027 maturity wall refinanced to 2032 in May 2026, and a maintained $0.45 quarterly dividend (~4.8% yield, paid on schedule July 28, 2026). Two overlays add asymmetry. First, hard assets: the Brazil forestlands were appraised at almost 5 billion reais (~$900 million) in late 2025 — nearly 60% of the whole market capitalization — and management quietly negotiated the payment owed to International Paper on any forestland sale down from $100 million to $85 million while publicly vowing never to sell, which keeps the monetization door oiled. Second, governance: Atlas Holdings holds roughly 21.5% economic exposure, terminated its cooperation agreement in November 2025, and the board's one-year poison pill expires November 9, 2026 — after which a full activist push or a bid becomes structurally possible, on a company whose own buyback average last year was $44.74. Conditions that must hold: Eastover lands on time in the fourth quarter, second-half price realization outruns oil-driven input inflation, and Latin American demand stays roughly flat.
bear_thesis: This is a shrinking commodity business printing its worst numbers since the spin, with the scoreboard removed. Uncoated freesheet demand declines roughly 3-5% a year on digitization — management's own 'real demand' framing concedes it — so every dollar of recovery must outrun a melting base. The near-term tape is guided to be ugly: first-quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $29 million (a 4% margin, down from $125 million the prior quarter), adjusted earnings per share were negative $0.53, trailing-twelve-month free cash flow is just $10 million against a $74 million annual dividend bill, and management told analysts the second quarter (printing August 7) 'will look similar.' The revival thesis leans on stable input costs at exactly the wrong moment: Brent is up roughly 24% off early July on the renewed Hormuz blockade, and management had already flagged rising energy, chemicals, diesel and ocean freight for the second quarter before the latest escalation — the same cost lines that are supposed to stay tame while second-half price increases stick. Forensic quality is middling: guidance was withdrawn entirely at the cycle trough (February 2026), the earnings-beat rate is 3 of 7 quarters, 'one-off' reliability failures have now recurred in consecutive first quarters (North America in 2025, Europe and Brazil in 2026, a debarking drum unfixed until the fourth quarter), insiders show zero open-market buys against seven sells, and capital allocation bought $42 million of stock at an average of $44.74 then paused entirely in the high $30s. Europe has run below its cost of capital for three years with only a 2027 aspiration to fix it, and the board answered its largest shareholder's board exit with a poison pill within five days — a bid deterrent, not a value catalyst, until at least November 2026. If 2027 EBITDA only reaches ~$380 million because Europe keeps bleeding and inflation eats the price increases, the stock is worth low-$20s and the 'cheapness' was a value trap on a structurally shrinking base. consensus_delta: There is barely a consensus to arbitrage — only one price target printed last quarter (Truist at $51 on July 15, 2026, with the stock at $38.94), so the '36% upside to consensus' in the screener is one analyst's opinion, not a street view. The $29 million first-quarter EBITDA embeds ~$65 million of one-time, fully disclosed transition costs plus a deliberate inventory build; treating 2026 as run-rate ignores that management pre-announced this as 'a year of two halves' and has hit every self-issued quarterly EBITDA range it ever gave. (2) The bullish error — the thin street is underpricing the oil shock's direct hit to the recovery math. # Sylvamo (SLVM) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-10-12 from five earnings calls (Q2 2025, 2025-08-08, through Q2 2026, 2026-08-07) cross-checked against the screener's financial history and the 2026-06-30 balance sheet. Live price used: $30.92 (NYSE, USD, FMP quote 2026-10-12), a fresh 52-week low.*

**Bottom line:** Sylvamo is a focused uncoated freesheet (office and printing paper) producer with genuinely low-cost Brazilian mills and owned forest land, now in a self-declared "transition year". Management has been honest about the bad news, but it has a pattern of over-promising on price and timing, it has withdrawn first annual and then quarterly earnings guidance, and the whole investment case now leans on a second-half 2026 recovery that has not yet shown up in reported numbers. The next quarterly report on 2026-11-06 is the first real test.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q2 2025 (2025-08-08):** a confident, cash-return story under retiring CEO Jean-Michel Ribieras. Net debt was 1.3x adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation, adjusted for one-offs), $40M was returned to shareholders in the quarter, and Q3 adjusted EBITDA was guided to $145-165M. The Eastover (South Carolina) investment programme of $145M was introduced as the growth engine.
- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-07):** delivered $151M of adjusted EBITDA, inside guidance, and bought back $42M of stock at an average $44.74, exhausting the authorisation; a new $150M authorisation followed. But the story picked up two new problems: International Paper would convert its Riverdale mill (Sylvamo's contracted supply of roughly 260,000 tons a year) to containerboard, ending supply in May 2026; and the largest shareholder, Atlas Holdings, pulled its two directors, ending the cooperation agreement. Management began talking up the Brazilian forest land (appraised at almost BRL 5 billion) as hidden value.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-13):** new CEO John Sims opened with a "Sylvamo will be legendary" vision statement, dropped quarterly EBITDA guidance (annual guidance was already dropped in 2024), paused buybacks, and labelled 2026 a "transition year". 2025 closed at $448M adjusted EBITDA and only $44M of free cash flow, while $155M was returned to shareholders - about 350% of free cash flow.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-05-08):** the trough. Adjusted EBITDA fell to $29M (4% margin), adjusted earnings were minus $0.53 a share, reliability problems in Europe and Brazil cost about $9M, and a $10M one-off gas charge came via Riverdale. Refinancing pushed the 2027 term loan out to 2032. A lean-manufacturing programme was launched.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-08-07):** a partial rebound to $60M adjusted EBITDA (7% margin), free cash flow minus $23M. Management now frames the year as "a tale of two halves", guiding a $75-85M better price-and-mix contribution in the second half, and calls the first half "the nadir".

The arc moves from "strong balance sheet, return cash" to "transition, invest, trust the long-term targets" - greater than $300M of annual free cash flow and a 15% return on invested capital (ROIC), with no date attached.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong financial position" (every call) | Net debt rose to $841M at 2026-06-30 against trailing-twelve-month adjusted EBITDA of roughly $365M (151 + 125 + 29 + 60) - about 2.3x, up from 1.3x in mid-2025 | Still manageable, but clearly weaker; the claim is getting stale |

Across 2021-2025, revenue went $2.83B to $3.35B but net income fell from $331M to $132M and earnings per share from $7.52 to $3.22. Gross margin is about 22% and contracting. Quarterly EBITDA ranges were met while they existed (Q2, Q3, Q4 2025). Softer promises - price realisation, Eastover timing, the Riverdale bridge - have slipped or been re-cut. Red: leverage rising to about 2.6x with thin free cash flow; paying to exit Europe; guidance withdrawn; insiders sold 12,980 shares in the open market with no buys; Piotroski 3/9; structurally shrinking end market (industry North America demand about -2% this year); imports rising again.
